findings.issue_text: isTeamAdminOrOwner uses && instead of ||, so users must be both admin and owner (effectively only owner) to pass; team admins are wrongly denied

No max length on guests array and server-side schema doesn't enforce uniqueness (only validated client-side), allowing unbounded/duplicate emails to spam emails and create duplicate attendee rows

Duplicate detection is case-sensitive: guest === attendee.email, and blacklisted emails are lowercased while input guests are not, so User@x.com vs user@x.com bypasses attendee-dedupe and blacklist; emails should be normalized before comparison and storage

bookingAttendees.attendees includes ALL attendees (existing + new) so sendAddGuestsEmails and evt.attendees resend to existing attendees too; combined with missing intra-input dedupe, duplicate emails create duplicate attendee rows and calendar/ICS updates

goldens.comment: The addGuests.handler.ts blacklist check uses blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest) after lowercasing the blacklist but not the input guest emails, allowing attackers to bypass BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS restrictions by submitting emails with uppercase characters.

The logic for checking team admin/owner permissions is incorrect. This condition uses AND (&&) which requires both isTeamAdmin AND isTeamOwner to be true, but it should use OR (||) since a user needs to be either an admin OR an owner to have permission.

The sendAddGuestsEmails function in email-manager.ts passes the full calendarEvent.attendees array when determining which attendees receive AttendeeScheduledEmail vs AttendeeAddGuestsEmail, but checks if newGuests.includes(attendee.email) where newGuests is the input guests array.

uniqueGuests filters out existing attendees and blacklisted emails but does not deduplicate duplicates within the input; createMany can insert duplicate attendee rows if the client submits repeated emails.
Starting with an array containing an empty string may cause validation issues. Consider starting with an empty array [] and handling the empty state in the MultiEmail component instead.

The `sendAddGuestsEmails` function does not check the `disableStandardEmails` flags in the `EventType` metadata, which may result in sending emails to hosts/attendees even when standard emails are disabled for the event type.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Any existing attendee (isAttendee) is granted permission to mutate the booking, add guests, trigger calendar updates and mass emails, enabling email/calendar abuse by arbitrary bookers

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts the authorization gate explicitly allows any attendee to proceed: `const isAttendee = !!booking.attendees.find((attendee) => attendee.email === user.email);` and it only throws FORBIDDEN if `!isTeamAdminOrOwner && !isOrganizer && !isAttendee`. That means any existing attendee (booker/guest) can call `viewer.bookings.addGuests`, which then (1) mutates the booking by `prisma.booking.update(... attendees.createMany ...)`, (2) calls `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)` to push calendar updates, and (3) calls `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` which sends emails to organizer/team members and all attendees. This matches the finding: an arbitrary attendee can add guests and trigger calendar/email notifications, enabling abuse/spam.

adjudication_records.issue_text: eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees is called with the stale booking object fetched before the attendee update, so the calendar provider may not see newly added attendees

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts, the code updates attendees via prisma.booking.update(...) into bookingAttendees (which includes the new attendees), but then calls eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking) using the earlier `booking` fetched before the update. While it is true that `booking` is stale with respect to attendees, the proposed impact (“calendar provider may not see newly added attendees”) is not verifiable from this diff because `evt.attendees` is built from `bookingAttendees.attendees` (so the new guests are present in the CalendarEvent), and we can’t see whether updateCalendarAttendees relies on booking.attendees vs evt.attendees. Thus the finding’s stated problem is speculative based on code not shown here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Email send failures are swallowed with console.log only (no logger, no error context, no user feedback), so guests can be persisted without notification and caller still gets success

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts`, email sending is wrapped in `try { await sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests); } catch (err) { console.log("Error sending AddGuestsEmails"); }` and the error is neither rethrown nor returned/handled. The handler then returns `{ message: "Guests added" }` regardless. This means guests are persisted (and calendar attendees updated) even if notification emails fail, with no user-facing error and only a minimal `console.log` without the error object/context.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No check on booking status; guests can be added to cancelled/rejected bookings, generating confirmed emails/ICS for events that don't exist

adjudication.rationale: The new `addGuestsHandler` fetches the booking by `id` and proceeds to (1) append attendees in DB (`prisma.booking.update(... attendees.createMany ...)`), (2) call `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)`, and (3) send emails with ICS payloads that hardcode `status: "CONFIRMED"` in both `attendee-add-guests-email.ts` and `organizer-add-guests-email.ts`. There is no check of any booking status/state (e.g., cancelled/rejected) before performing these actions. Therefore, if a cancelled/rejected booking is passed (still exists in DB), the endpoint would still add guests and generate “confirmed” emails/ICS for it.

adjudication_records.issue_text: prisma.user.findFirstOrThrow({ where: { id: booking.userId || 0 } }) throws an unhandled NotFoundError (500) for bookings with no userId instead of a proper TRPCError

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuestsHandler`, the organizer is fetched with `prisma.user.findFirstOrThrow({ where: { id: booking.userId || 0 } })`. If `booking.userId` is `null/undefined` (which is plausible given the defensive `|| 0`), this queries `id: 0` and `findFirstOrThrow` will throw a Prisma NotFoundError. That exception is not caught or converted to a `TRPCError`, so it will propagate as an internal error (500) instead of a controlled TRPC error response. This is a concrete failure mode introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: isInvalidEmail in AddGuestsDialog is never cleared when the user edits emails or retries, so the error banner persists after input becomes valid; only Cancel resets it

adjudication.rationale: In `AddGuestsDialog`, `isInvalidEmail` is set to `true` when `ZAddGuestsInputSchema.safeParse(multiEmailValue)` fails in `handleAdd()`, but it is only reset to `false` in the Cancel button handler. There is no reset when the user edits the email fields (`MultiEmail` only updates `multiEmailValue`) or when a subsequent valid submission succeeds (`onSuccess` resets `multiEmailValue` and closes the dialog, but does not call `setIsInvalidEmail(false)`). Since the component stays mounted (rendered in `BookingListItem` regardless of open state), the error banner can persist even after the input becomes valid or after reopening the dialog unless Cancel was clicked.

adjudication_records.issue_text: MultiEmail.tsx uses array index as React key for list items that can be spliced/reordered, causing state/DOM mismatches when removing an email

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/ui/form/MultiEmail.tsx`, the list is rendered with `value.map((field, index) => <li key={index}>...)` while items can be removed via `updatedValue.splice(index, 1)`. When removing an email that is not the last item, all subsequent items shift indices, so React reuses component instances/DOM nodes for different emails. With input components (`EmailField`) this can lead to observable UI/state issues (e.g., focus/cursor jumping, validation state sticking to the wrong row) because identity is tied to the unstable index key.
